correctness.rationale: The complete bipartite stable-set inequalities give a full-dimensional normal lattice polytope by an explicit independent-set integer decomposition. Each active facet normal is a node-edge incidence column in a graph with two deleted boundary-node rows; no active path can join the boundary nodes. Total unimodularity gives saturated divisor presentation and torsion-free cokernel. Cycles occur exclusively in a lower K_{p+1,b}, upper K_{q+1,a}, or interior K_{r,s}; their cycle ranks give exactly the stated local class groups. The dual toric exact sequence makes rank zero equivalent to smoothness and Q-factoriality. Exact finite face enumeration cross-checks every face in six small parameter pairs, but generality rests on the symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: The global class group and local-Cartier test of Friedl, and singular-orbit methods of Lakshmibai–Mukherjee, are acknowledged as known. Prior singular-component/generic germ descriptions cover certain generic-orbit special cases but do not give the complete local group formula at nongeneric orbits or the full Q-factorial stratification. The assessed theorem calculates all orbitwise local groups, the lack of local torsion, and the exact global-to-maximal-local rank gap. A general toric divisor algorithm can in principle derive these with additional computations; unindexed equivalent specialization remains a genuine risk.

value.rationale: Local Weil-divisor class groups measure precisely failure of local factoriality and detect potential Q-factorial modifications. The result gives the entire orbitwise class-group rank distribution, not merely fixed-point samples or generic singular components, across an infinite natural family. Torsion-freeness has a concrete geometric consequence: every non-smooth point is non-Q-factorial. The largest local rank is ab-min(a,b), strictly below Friedl’s global rank ab, quantifying information lost on localization. The boundary/interior cases include higher intersections requiring actual combinatorial analysis rather than just a textbook definition.
